To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the genotoxic potential of MCYST‐ LR and NOD in vitro and in rat liver cells is due to their capacity to enhance 8‐oxoguanine formation in DNA.
MCYST‐LR (2 and 20 ng/ml) and NOD (1 and 10 ng/ml) induced oxidative DNA damage in primary cultured hepatocyte and in vivo in liver cells.

MCYST‐LR (2 and 20 ng/mL) and NOD (5 and 10 ng/ml) significantly enhanced 8 ‐ oxo‐dG levels in a time‐ and dose ‐ dependent manner in primary cultured rat liver cells and in rat liver cells, but did not induce DNA hydrophobic adduction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of cyanobacterial hepatotoxic microcystins and nodularins on DNA integrity.
the genotoxic potential of MCYST‐ LR and NOD in vitro in primary rat hepatocytes and also in vivo in rat livers.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genotoxic effects of MCYST‐ LR and nodularin on DNA are very limited and that these toxins do not seem to induce genotoxicity by the formation of DNA adducts.
the genotoxicity of MCYST‐ LR and NOD is not due to the formation of hydrophobic DNA‐adducts but rather is due to the induction of oxidative damage.

MCYST‐LR is a genotoxic agent that can induce both oxidative DNA damage and the formation of DNA adducts in primary cultured rat liver cells in vitro and in the liver of the rats in vivo, whereas NOD is a genotoxic hepatotoxin in primary cultured rat hepatic cells in vitro and the liver in vivo, but not a hepatocarcinogen in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MCYST‐LR (and NOD) could not induce hydrophobic adduction to DNA in vitro in primary hepatocytes.

The main takeaway from our work is that
we were able to demonstrate that MCYST‐LR is a potent genotoxin, inducing DNA damage in vitro in cultured hepatocytes and also in vivo in rat livers.
the depletion of I compounds and the formation of 8‐OH‐dG by MCYST‐Lr and NOD could contribute to hepatocarcinogenesis during long‐term exposures to these cyanobacteria toxins.
